newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: China CNPC plans $3.5 bln pipeline from Kazakhstan.
newsitem.headline: China CNPC plans $3.5 bln pipeline from Kazakhstan.

text.p: The Chinese National Petroleum Company (CNPC) plans to build an oil pipeline to China from Western Kazakhstan at an estimated cost of $3.5 billion, a senior CNPC official told a news conference on Wednesday.

"We intend to build an oil pipeline from Kazakhstan to China...according to our estimates, this will need investment of $3.5 billion," CNPC Vice President Wu Yaowen said. The pipeline is part of CNPC's deal to buy 60 percent of Kazakhstan's Aktyubinskmunaigaz oil company, signed on Wednesday.
Earlier, Kazakhstan said on Wednesday that CNPC had won a 60 percent stake in its large Aktyubinsk oil enterprise, with CNPC promising to pay $4.325 billion in investment and bonuses.

"The inter-departmental commission for privatisation of the Republic of Kazakhstan, after considering competitors' offers, has chosen the Chinese National Petroleum Company as the winner of the tender," said a statement given to reporters by the ex-Soviet state's privatisation committee.
"The overall value of the deal is $4.325 billion," it said.

U.S. oil majors Texaco Inc and Amoco Corp along with Russian company Yuzhny Most competed against CNPC in the tender. The committee said earlier that U.S. company Exxon dropped out of the competition.

Under the deal, CNPC has promised to invest $4 billion in the enterprise over the next 20 years, with $585 million to be invested from 1998 to 2003. CNPC will pay the Kazakh government a $320 million bonus along with a signing bonus of $5 million.
